question_text: A program repeatedly accesses a working set that is larger than its current CPU cache. Explain why a larger cache might improve its runtime.
adaptation_rationale: Original application rewritten to be self-contained; assessed reasoning retained within cited 2027 scope.
solution: The larger cache can retain more of the repeatedly accessed data/instructions.; This can increase the cache-hit rate and reduce accesses to slower RAM.; The CPU spends less time waiting for memory, reducing runtime; improvement depends on the access pattern.
